safetyClassNote: read-only means: changes no tracked file, remote, or registry. It may update remote-tracking git refs and write logs and receipts under .trellis.

tools.name: gates
tools.description: Runs the root and desktop typecheck and unit tests (and optionally e2e and the desktop build), stops at the first failure, and reports counts and the first failing line instead of the log.

args.name: --only NAMES
args.description: Comma list of steps to run: root-typecheck, root-test, desktop-typecheck, desktop-test, desktop-e2e, desktop-build. With --e2e or --build, the list must name the matching step.

args.name: --e2e
args.description: Also run desktop-e2e under the machine-wide lock; refuses if the lock is held.

args.name: --build
args.description: Also run desktop-build (electron-builder; heavy).

args.name: --clean
args.description: After the run, remove only the allowlisted build outputs (including the root dist; not the installers) and report the bytes freed. A path it refuses, such as a symlink, makes the run fail with exit 1.

args.name: --clean-installers
args.description: After the run, also remove apps/desktop/release, the installers. Run it after release verify has passed: it refuses (exit 1) unless release/desktop-sha256.json exists, names the version in release/beta.json, and records the real SHA-256 of every installer.

args.name: --min-free-gib N
args.description: Raise the free-disk floor above 12 GiB; it can never be lowered.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout, also for a usage error.

output.note: Each step has name, command, cwd, exitCode, passed, reason, ms, rawBytes, counts, firstFailure, and log. A reason is null, TIME_LIMIT, LOG_LIMIT, START_FAILED, NO_SUMMARY, TEST_FAILURES, or NO_TESTS_RAN. clean has removed, refused, freedBytes, and error. Full logs, with secrets redacted, are in .trellis/gates/<step>.log. A usage error or crash prints {ok:false, exit:2, error} instead.

tools.name: lane-tree
tools.description: Creates, lists, and safely removes the separate working copy for one lane of work; list only reads, and remove is a dry run unless --apply is given.

args.name: create|remove|list
args.description: The subcommand.

args.name: --name SLUG
args.description: create: the lane name, lower-case letters, digits, and dashes.

args.name: --base REF
args.description: create: the base branch (origin/ and refs/heads/ prefixes allowed) or a 40-character commit id, such as origin/release/0.8.0-beta.2. HEAD is not allowed.

args.name: --dest ABS_PATH
args.description: create and remove: the absolute folder of the lane tree.

args.name: --branch NAME
args.description: create: the lane branch (default task/<slug>).

args.name: --modules-from ABS_CHECKOUT
args.description: create: copy node_modules and apps/desktop/node_modules from this checkout, copy-on-write, on macOS only.

args.name: --min-free-gib N
args.description: create: raise the free-disk floor above 12 GiB; it can never be lowered.

args.name: --apply
args.description: remove: delete the folder; without it the command only reports what it would delete. It reads the status, HEAD, and stash again just before it deletes and refuses if they changed. It refuses a lane whose branch was squash-merged and deleted on origin (its commits are not on origin); delete that one by hand.

args.name: --root ABS_DIR
args.description: list: the folder to look in (default: the folder that holds this repository).

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout, also for a usage error.

output.note: Each subcommand puts only the keys marked for it in the result. When --modules-from copies nothing, ok stays true and modulesCopied is false with a modulesNote. A usage error or crash prints {ok:false, exit:2, error} instead.

tools.name: public-scan
tools.description: Scans the added lines of the net diff and of every commit patch, the file paths, commit messages, author names, and the HEAD blob of each added binary file of a branch, and optionally its pull request text, for home paths, session links, emails, secrets, and private terms, and checks the pull request shape.

args.name: --base REF
args.description: The base to diff against (default origin/release/0.8.0-beta.2).

args.name: --pr-body FILE
args.description: Check the pull request text: alert opener first, at most 300 words, no leaks.

args.name: --terms-file ABS_FILE
args.description: A file outside the repository with one private term per line; findings never print a term. A file with no terms is an error.

args.name: --allow-empty
args.description: Accept a range with no commits or nothing added; without it an empty range exits 1. The output then says it was accepted, never clean.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout, also for a usage error.

output.note: Each finding has kind, file, line, excerpt, and for a term the termLine in the terms file; a finding on a line that only an earlier commit patch added (it was removed again later) also has commit. A path finding has the file file-path and the position of the path in git diff --name-only as its line. A finding inside a binary file has that file and the line 0. addedLines counts the net diff and patchLines every commit patch. A line over 4000 characters is scanned in overlapping 4000-character windows, never skipped. binaryScanned names the binary files scanned from their HEAD blob (a name that matches a leak pattern is shown as [path withheld]); unscanned lists { file, reason } for a binary file over 5 MiB or unreadable, and makes the exit 1. termsChecked is null when no terms file was given. A usage error or crash prints {ok:false, exit:2, error} instead.

tools.name: release:status
tools.description: Show each release phase as done, todo, or unknown, with a reason.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: phases lists each release phase as { phase, state, reason }.

tools.name: release:preflight
tools.description: Fetch origin, then check branch, sync with origin, and a clean tree. Print the commit.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --branch
args.description: NAME. The branch the release must be on.

output.note: checks lists { name, status, detail } for fetch, branch, commit, sync, and clean.

tools.name: release:gates
tools.description: Run the gate commands from the config in order. Stop at the first failure.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --force
args.description: Run the gates again even if a passing receipt exists for this commit.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --e2e
args.description: Also run the end-to-end gate.

args.name: --min-free-gib
args.description: N. Raise the free-disk floor; it can never be lowered.

output.note: receipt is the receipt written under .trellis (its seams key lists any test seams in use); ran names the gates run. gate, log, gates, freeGiB, and floorGiB appear only when the step fails, and commit, ran, and receipt only when it passes; the keys in output.optional can be absent.

tools.name: release:dry-run
tools.description: Pack the tarball and run npm publish --dry-run on it. Report size, count, SHA-256, and integrity.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --force
args.description: Run the dry run again even if a passing receipt exists for this commit.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --min-free-gib
args.description: N. Raise the free-disk floor; it can never be lowered.

output.note: The tarball, sha256, and integrity are those of the packed file; entries counts every entry in the tarball, bundled files included. log and entry appear only when the step fails (entry names the tarball entry that must never ship).

tools.name: release:publish
tools.description: Print the publish commands for a person to run. Never runs them.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: A human-only subcommand: it prints commands and runs nothing. Without a terminal the outcome is refused and the exit is 2. commit appears when a dry-run receipt is found.

tools.name: release:hashes
tools.description: Write the SHA-256 of each desktop artifact to the hash file. Every artifact name must contain the release version.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --force
args.description: Replace an existing hash file even when its version or a recorded hash differs.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: files maps each desktop artifact name to its SHA-256. different, found, and stale appear only when the step fails (found lists the artifacts on disk; stale lists the ones whose name lacks the release version).

tools.name: release:verify
tools.description: Check the registry tag and integrity, an install from the registry, and the desktop hashes.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --tarball
args.description: PATH. A local tarball to compare with the registry.

output.note: checks lists { name, status, reason } for dist-tag, integrity, install, and desktop-sha256.

tools.name: release:tag
tools.description: Create the annotated git tag on the checked commit. Does not push.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

args.name: --commit
args.description: HASH. The full 40-character commit to tag.

args.name: --branch
args.description: NAME. The branch the release must be on.

output.note: The tag is created locally and never pushed. existing appears only when the tag already points at another commit.

tools.name: release:push-tag
tools.description: Print the git push command for the tag. Never runs it.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: A human-only subcommand: it prints the command and runs nothing.

tools.name: release:retire
tools.description: Print the npm deprecate and dist-tag commands from the config. Never runs them.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: A human-only subcommand: it prints the commands and runs nothing.

tools.name: release:claims
tools.description: Scan the configured files for stale wording. Exit 1 on any hit.

args.name: --json
args.description: Print exactly one JSON object on stdout.

args.name: --repo
args.description: DIR. Run against another repository root.

output.note: hits lists file:line positions of stale wording. missing appears only when a configured file is absent.

tools.name: check-test-patterns
tools.description: Fails when a test or test:* script of package.json lists a node --test pattern that matches no file.

output.note: Exit 1 and a list on stderr when a pattern matches nothing; run it after a build, because some patterns name dist/ files.

tools.name: check-test-temp-cleanup
tools.description: Fails when a test file makes a temp folder with mkdtemp and has no removal that runs after the test.

tools.name: check-not-built
tools.description: Fails while a contract stub that throws "not built" is left in a file that ships.

tools.name: check-social-preview
tools.description: Checks the social card tags in the built landing and documentation pages and the size of both card images; needs the built apps.

tools.name: render-social-preview
tools.description: Redraws the home and documentation social card images with playwright-cli and replaces the committed PNG files only after both pass.

output.note: Writes apps/landing/public/social/*.png and a scratch folder under .trellis/; needs playwright-cli and its Chromium.

tools.name: docs-visuals:capture-shots
tools.description: Takes the desktop documentation screenshots again under the machine-wide e2e lock and updates the shots half of the visuals manifest.

args.name: DOCS_SHOTS_ONLY
args.description: Environment variable: a comma list of shot ids to take.

output.note: Builds the root packages first; writes WebP files to apps/docs/public/visuals.

tools.name: docs-visuals:capture-terminals
tools.description: Records the real output of each terminal entry of the plan against a sample project in a private temporary home and writes it to the visuals manifest.

output.note: Needs the CLI built first (npm run build at the root); writes apps/docs/src/visuals/manifest.json.

tools.name: docs-visuals:manifest-shots
tools.description: Writes the shots half of the visuals manifest from the plan and the size of each light WebP file.

output.note: Writes apps/docs/src/visuals/manifest.json.

tools.name: verify
tools.description: Runs the typecheck, the regression tests, the landing build, and a production dependency audit in order, and writes a JSON record per check.

args.name: BOWERLOOM_RELEASE_GATE
args.description: Environment variable: set to 1 to run the not-built check first.

output.note: Prints one JSON line per check and writes logs and report.json to .trellis/verification/; the audit reads the npm registry.

tools.name: run-node-tests
tools.description: Runs node --test with the given arguments in its own process group under a wall-clock limit, and kills the group past the limit.

args.name: NODE_TEST_ARGUMENTS
args.description: The node --test arguments, without --test.

args.name: BOWERLOOM_TEST_WALL_LIMIT_SECONDS
args.description: Environment variable: lowers the 45 minute limit; it can never raise it.

output.note: Exit 124 on the time limit; the tests it runs may write temp files.
